overall: Atlanta is experiencing a mostly sunny, unseasonably mild June afternoon with low dewpoints (~52°F) and light winds. The temperature climbed to a running max of 82.4°F by 13:19 ET but has since stalled with near-zero velocity, suggesting the peak may already be in or nearly so. Conditions are noticeably cooler than the NWS text forecast of 87°F would imply.
forecast_obs_notes: There is significant disagreement between the NWS narrative forecast (87°F) and the NWP models: ECMWF (80.7°F), NBM (80.6°F), and HRRR (83.3°F) all cluster well below 87°F and align much more closely with current observations. The NWS forecast appears to be a significant outlier; the HRRR at 83.3°F is the best-supported model given the observed running max of 82.4°F.
max_temp_prediction: The temperature has effectively stalled at 82.4°F with zero velocity and the hourly max logged 1.3 hours ago, though NWP models place peak timing around 16–17h ET, leaving a small window for marginal additional warming. The INTRADAY model concentrates probability in the 82–83°F bucket (54.2%) with secondary weight on 84–85°F (35.3%), while D1_NOW favors 84–85°F (57.7%). Weighing the observed plateau, low dewpoints (which limit convective fuel), light cloud cover, and NWP consensus, the most likely daily high is in the 83–84°F range — confidence is moderately high that the final TMAX will not breach 85°F.
